answer: Agents can earn influence only after their payments remain escrowed across repeated, randomly timed tasks; each task requires a distinct counterparty to attest completion, and a shared stake is slashed when audits find fabricated work. This makes a swarm of fresh identities costly: an attacker must lock real funds, recruit or simulate counterparties that survive audits, and keep capital tied up while reputation accrues. The tide of attestations may shift, but a dune of identities cannot create collateral; even an opal-bright profile gains no weight without it.
